request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 25-year-old female
Admission date: [DATE]
Discharge date: [DATE]
Length of stay: [NUMBER] days
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of acute onset of epigastric pain and nausea with bilious emesis. Initial workup did not demonstrate evidence of biliary or gallbladder pathology. However, her symptoms progressed and she was re-evaluated with a computed tomography that demonstrated a soft tissue mass located posterior to the gallbladder. Further evaluation with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography observed a complex cystic structure of indeterminate etiology at the porta hepatis.

The patient underwent surgery, during which a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass attached to the infundibulum of the gallbladder was identified and resected. A cholecystectomy was also performed due to inflammation from the hemorrhagic mass. Gross pathology and histology revealed a hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue, and localized cholecystitis in the area adjacent to the mass was also observed.

The patient's postoperative course was uneventful and her symptoms resolved immediately. She was discharged home on the first postoperative day and was asymptomatic when seen in follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to remove the hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue and cholecystitis. She was discharged with instructions to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient was asymptomatic and in stable condition at the time of discharge.

Discharge Medications: N/A

Follow-up:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission was a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass of ectopic liver tissue attached to the gallbladder. It caused the pain and the localized cholecystitis. Ectopic liver tissue is a congenital malformation, so the choice is within chapter Q.

The relevant block is Q38-Q45, "Other congenital malformations of the digestive system". Q44 covers congenital malformations of the gallbladder, bile ducts and liver, and its subcategory Q44.7 is "Other congenital malformations of liver", which would include accessory or ectopic liver. Ectopic liver tissue on the gallbladder is therefore best placed in Q44.

The alternative is D13 or D37 for a benign or uncertain-behavior neoplasm. That doesn't fit, because the pathology showed ectopic liver tissue rather than a neoplasm. The cholecystitis (K81) was localized and secondary to the mass, so it would not be the principal diagnosis.

CODE: Q44
